meta.title: Nazar Vision — Computer vision & robot perception for business
meta.description: We build computer vision systems that count, inspect, read and guide robots — for manufacturing, textiles, logistics, retail and more. Try our live demos in your browser.

hero.title: Put the cameras you already have to work
hero.subtitle: We build computer vision for factories, warehouses and shops: safety alerts, counting, quality checks and document reading. It runs on your cameras and your servers.
hero.note: No sign-up. The demos run in your browser, so your images stay on your device.

oss.text: Our library tracks 80+ open-source computer vision and robotics projects with live GitHub data and licence checks. Some of the most popular models are AGPL-licensed, which can force you to open your own code. We flag that for you.

items.title: Failed-case report

risks.title: Why vision projects fail, and what we do about it

items.risk: 98% in the lab, 70% on the floor
items.fix: We collect test images on your site, at different times of day and on different shifts, before we promise any accuracy.
Labelling is quoted up front, and AI-assisted annotation with human review cuts the hours.
We fix the scene first. Camera position, lens and lighting are cheaper than a bigger model.
Safety and quality decisions keep a person in the loop, with confidence thresholds you approve.
We don’t put AGPL models in closed products, and every licence is listed in the handover.

needs.title: What we need from you
items: 20–50 example photos or a short video of the real scene
One person who knows the process and can answer questions
A clear rule for what counts as good and bad
Today’s numbers: units per hour, staff on checks, current miss rate
Access to one camera, or permission to install a test camera

hardware.compare: For comparison, all-in-one AI inspection cameras from specialist vendors list at about $4,500–13,500 per unit. Standard cameras sharing one edge computer usually cost a fraction of that.

roi.title: Will it pay for itself?

fields.inspectors: People on visual checks, per shift

demos.title: Live computer vision, in your browser
demos.subtitle: Each demo downloads a model once and runs it on your device. Use your webcam, upload a photo or pick a sample.

object-detection.title: Object detection
object-detection.short: Find and label 80 types of everyday objects. Switch between a real-time model and a more accurate one.
object-detection.business: Basis for counting products, vehicles, tools or people, on a live camera or recorded video.

people-counter.title: Line counter
people-counter.short: Draw a line and count people, cars or bottles crossing it in each direction.
people-counter.business: Footfall for shops and offices, traffic counts, and units passing on a conveyor.

face-anonymizer.title: Face anonymiser
face-anonymizer.short: Detect faces and blur them automatically — privacy by design.

pose-estimation.title: Pose estimation
pose-estimation.short: Track 33 body keypoints to understand posture and motion.
pose-estimation.business: Ergonomics, fall detection, fitness and sports.

hand-gestures.title: Hand gestures
hand-gestures.short: Recognise hand gestures and track 21 points per hand.

ocr.title: Text recognition (OCR)
ocr.short: Read printed text from photos in English, Uzbek and Russian.

barcode-scanner.title: Barcode & QR scanner
barcode-scanner.short: Read QR, EAN, Code 128, DataMatrix and more.

background-removal.title: Background removal
background-removal.short: Cut out people and products for clean catalogue photos.

defect-check.title: Zero-shot quality check
defect-check.short: Type your own labels — e.g. “scratched” vs “clean” — and the model judges the image.
defect-check.business: Quick feasibility test for inspection before custom training.

depth-estimation.title: Depth estimation
depth-estimation.short: Estimate how far every pixel is from the camera, from one photo.
depth-estimation.business: Volume estimation, robotics and spatial analytics.

safety-zone.title: Danger zone alert
safety-zone.short: Mark an area next to a machine or forklift lane. An alarm fires the moment a person steps in.
safety-zone.business: Worker safety near presses, robots, conveyors and forklift routes. Logs every breach with its duration.

ppe-check.title: PPE check
ppe-check.short: Type what workers must wear: helmet, vest, gloves. The model finds each item and flags who is missing it.
ppe-check.business: Safety compliance on factory floors, construction sites and warehouses, with no custom training for a first pilot.

fatigue-monitor.title: Operator fatigue
fatigue-monitor.short: Tracks eye closure, blinks and yawns on a face, and warns about drowsiness and microsleep.
fatigue-monitor.business: Truck, bus and forklift drivers, crane and control-room operators on long shifts.

segment-anything.title: Segment anything
segment-anything.short: Click any object to cut it out with a pixel-accurate mask, then measure or download it.
segment-anything.business: Measuring parts and defects, building training data in minutes, and robot grasping.

movement-heatmap.title: Movement heatmap
movement-heatmap.short: See where people or vehicles spend their time. The longer the video runs, the clearer the busy spots and empty corners.
movement-heatmap.business: Store layout and product placement, warehouse aisle use, bottlenecks on the shop floor, where to put a new camera or sign.

queue-dwell.title: Queue and wait time
queue-dwell.short: Mark a till, counter or doorway. See how many people wait there and for how long, with an alert when the queue gets too long.
queue-dwell.business: Open another till before customers leave, measure service time at banks and clinics, check how long trucks wait at a gate.

vehicle-speed.title: Vehicle speed
vehicle-speed.short: Two lines and a known distance turn any camera into a speed check. Each car gets its own km/h, and speeders are flagged.
vehicle-speed.business: Speed control on factory and warehouse sites, residential streets and parking lots; traffic studies without radar.

image-enhance.title: Image enhance
image-enhance.short: Make a small or blurry CCTV frame twice as large and sharper, then compare before and after with a slider.
image-enhance.business: Readable details from old cameras, sharper evidence frames, better input for other models when the camera is far away.

scene-describe.title: Ask about a photo
scene-describe.short: One model that describes a scene in words, lists the objects in it, finds anything you type and reads the text.
scene-describe.business: Searchable camera archives, automatic incident notes, checking photos sent by field staff, and finding objects no detector was trained for.

ui.cameraDenied: Camera access was blocked or no camera was found. You can still upload a photo or use a sample.
ui.modelFailed: The model couldn’t be downloaded. Check your connection and try again.
ui.dropHint: Drop an image or video here, or click to choose
ui.firstLoad: First load downloads about {size}. After that it’s cached.
ui.drawLine: Click two points on the image to redraw the counting line.
ui.noCodes: No codes found. Try a sharper, closer photo.
ui.qualityNote: Best quality needs a WebGPU browser (recent Chrome or Edge).
ui.labelsHint: Describe each class in plain English, e.g. “fresh bread, burnt bread, moldy bread”.
ui.imageFailed: That image couldn’t be loaded. Try another file.
ui.videoFailed: That video couldn’t be played. Try an MP4 or WebM file.
ui.enginesNote: Real-time runs at video speed on most devices. High accuracy (RT-DETR) finds more small and crowded objects but updates less often on video.
ui.zoneDrawing: Click {n} more point(s) to finish the zone.
ui.zoneHint: Click 4 points on the image to draw your own zone. A person counts as inside when their feet are inside.
ui.ppeHint: Include “person” to check each worker. Head items (helmet) and torso items (vest, jacket) are matched to the person wearing them. Wording matters: “helmet” works better than “hard hat”. Zero-shot models can confuse similar items; a production system is fine-tuned on your own images.
ui.fatigueLiveOnly: Fatigue is measured over time: play a video or start the webcam. On a photo you see eye and mouth openness only.
ui.noFace: No face found. Face the camera with your whole face in view.
ui.perclosNote: PERCLOS is the share of the last 30 s with eyes closed, a standard drowsiness measure. A real system is tuned per camera and person.
ui.samHint: Click an object to select it. Add more points to grow the mask, or switch to Exclude to cut parts away.
ui.samEmpty: Click on the image to segment an object.
ui.pickSceneHint: Click a picture to run the model on it. The first run downloads {size}; after that it’s instant.
ui.heatNote: Positions are logged five times a second at the feet (people) or wheels (vehicles). In a real system this runs for days and is compared week to week.
ui.queueDraw: Click 4 points on the video to mark your own waiting area: a till, a counter, a doorway.
ui.speedDraw: Click 4 points to place line A and line B across the road, then set the real distance between them.
ui.speedNote: Accuracy depends on measuring that distance on the ground. A fixed, calibrated camera measures within a few km/h; this demo is an estimate.
ui.enhanceNote: The model makes details clearer but cannot recover what the camera never captured. Frames are kept small so it runs in a browser; expect 10–60 seconds on a laptop.
ui.askTask: What do you want to know?
ui.askNote: Answers are in English. On a computer without a modern graphics chip, each answer takes 10–40 seconds.

card.download: Runs in your browser. {size} download, once.

oss.title: The free computer vision toolbox, checked for business use
oss.subtitle: Star counts and activity come straight from GitHub. Licence badges tell you whether a project is safe to ship inside a commercial product.

licenseNote.title: Why licences matter
licenseNote.text: Permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) let you use a project inside closed-source products. AGPL and GPL can require you to publish your own source code — Ultralytics YOLO, the most popular detector, is AGPL-3.0 unless you buy an enterprise licence. Projects marked “unclear” use custom or research-only terms.

items.q: Do we need to buy new cameras?
items.a: Often not. Most IP cameras with an RTSP stream work. For precise inspection we may recommend an industrial camera and lighting — we tell you during discovery.

items.q: Where does our video and data go?
items.a: Wherever you decide. We can run everything on-premises or on edge devices with no internet. We sign an NDA before seeing your footage.
We measure it on your own data during the pilot and report precision and recall before you commit to a full deployment.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A pilot takes 2–4 weeks. A production deployment usually takes 1–3 months, depending on sites and integrations.

items.q: Do you use open-source models? Is that safe?
items.a: Yes, and we check every licence. We prefer commercially permissive models (Apache-2.0, MIT) and tell you when a model needs a paid licence.
Yes. We work remotely with clients worldwide, in English, Uzbek and Russian, and can travel for on-site installation.

items.q: Can you work with our robots?
items.a: Yes. We build ROS 2 perception and integrate with major robot brands through their SDKs or PLC I/O. We start with a free feasibility check on your real parts.

useCases.title: 36 jobs cameras can do for your business
useCases.subtitle: Concrete problems we see in factories, warehouses, shops and on the road, what a vision system does about them, and what to measure. Most start with a pilot of 2–4 weeks.
useCases.effortNote: Quick win: usually works with standard models and existing cameras. Standard: needs custom training on your images. Advanced: needs special cameras, lighting or 3D, and a longer pilot.
useCases.ctaTitle: Found your problem? Here’s how we start.

assembly.title: Assembly verification
assembly.problem: A missing screw, clip or cable is found only at final test, or by the customer.
assembly.how: A camera checks each unit at the station and confirms every part is present and in the right place.

surface.title: Surface defect inspection
surface.problem: Scratches, dents and stains are judged by tired eyes, differently on every shift.
surface.how: A model trained on your good and bad parts flags defects at line speed and saves an image of each.
surface.kpi: escape rate, false rejects, inspections per hour

fillLevel.title: Fill level and cap check
fillLevel.problem: Under-filled bottles and loose caps slip through and come back as complaints.
fillLevel.how: Each container is measured as it passes; out-of-spec units trigger a reject gate.

labelCheck.title: Label, date and batch code check
labelCheck.problem: A wrong label or an unreadable expiry date forces a recall.
labelCheck.how: OCR reads the printed text and compares it with the batch on the production order.

weld.title: Weld and seam inspection
weld.problem: Weld quality is checked by sampling, so bad joints reach assembly.
weld.how: Every weld is imaged and classified; doubtful ones are routed to a person.
weld.kpi: defects found per 1,000 welds, rework cost

dimensions.title: Dimension measurement
dimensions.problem: Parts are measured by hand with calipers on a small sample.
dimensions.how: A calibrated camera measures length, diameter or gaps on every part without contact.

packaging.title: Packaging integrity
packaging.problem: Crushed boxes, torn film and open flaps leave the plant.
packaging.how: Cameras at the end of the line check every pack before palletising.

conveyorCount.title: Conveyor counting
conveyorCount.problem: Output is counted by hand or by sensors that miss touching items.
conveyorCount.how: Vision counts units crossing a line, by product type, and reports output per hour.

machineZone.title: Machine danger zones
machineZone.problem: People step into press, robot or conveyor areas while machines run.
machineZone.how: A zone is drawn around the machine; an entry raises an alarm or slows the machine via the PLC.
machineZone.kpi: zone breaches per week, near misses

ppe.title: PPE compliance
ppe.problem: Hard hats, vests and gloves are checked only during audits.
ppe.how: Cameras at entrances and work areas flag missing PPE and send a photo to the shift lead.
ppe.kpi: compliance rate by area and shift

gauges.title: Analog gauge and meter reading
gauges.problem: Someone walks the plant to write down pressure, temperature and meter readings.
gauges.how: Cheap cameras read dials and counters and log values automatically, with alerts on limits.

fabric.title: Fabric defect detection
fabric.problem: Holes, stains and broken yarns are spotted late, after cutting.
fabric.how: Cameras over the loom or inspection table flag defects and log their position on the roll.

seams.title: Seam and stitch inspection
seams.problem: Skipped stitches and crooked seams are caught at final QC or not at all.
seams.how: Garments are imaged at the station; faulty seams are flagged before the next operation.

shade.title: Colour and shade matching
shade.problem: Shade differences between batches are judged by eye under shop lights.
shade.how: A controlled-light camera compares each batch with the approved reference.

garmentCount.title: Piece and bundle counting
garmentCount.problem: Piece-rate counts per worker are disputed and checked by hand.
garmentCount.how: Cameras count finished pieces per station and feed the payroll report.

binPicking.title: Bin picking
binPicking.problem: Robots can’t pick parts that lie jumbled in a bin, so a person feeds the line.
binPicking.how: 3D vision finds each part and its pose and gives the robot a safe grasp point.
binPicking.kpi: picks per hour, pick success rate

cobotSafety.title: Collaborative robot cell safety
cobotSafety.problem: Fences slow work, but without them people get too close to robots.
cobotSafety.how: Vision tracks people around the cell and slows or pauses the robot when someone comes near.

partPose.title: Part position for pick-and-place
partPose.problem: Fixtures must hold every part in exactly the same place.
partPose.how: A camera locates each part and corrects the robot’s path, so fixtures can be simpler.

dock.title: Dock and pallet monitoring
dock.problem: Nobody knows how long trucks wait or how many pallets were loaded.
dock.how: Cameras count pallets in and out and time each truck at the dock.

forkliftProximity.title: Forklift–pedestrian alerts
forkliftProximity.problem: Near misses between forklifts and people go unreported until someone is hurt.
forkliftProximity.how: Vision detects people in forklift lanes and alerts the driver and the supervisor.
forkliftProximity.kpi: near misses per week by zone

parcelSize.title: Parcel dimensioning
parcelSize.problem: Parcel sizes are typed in by hand, so shipping is billed wrongly.
parcelSize.how: A depth camera measures each parcel’s size on the conveyor or table.

scanTunnel.title: Barcode scan tunnel
scanTunnel.problem: Workers scan each box by hand, and damaged labels stop the line.
scanTunnel.how: Several cameras read every barcode on a moving box, from any side.

damage.title: Damaged goods at receiving
damage.problem: Damage is noticed after the supplier’s driver has left.
damage.how: Every incoming pallet is photographed and checked for damage, with images saved as evidence.

footfall.title: Footfall and conversion
footfall.problem: Shops know their sales, but not how many people walked in.
footfall.how: Entrance cameras count visitors in and out by hour, without storing faces.
footfall.kpi: visitors, conversion rate, staffing per hour

queues.title: Queue length alerts
queues.problem: Customers leave long queues before anyone opens another till.
queues.how: Vision counts people waiting and pings staff when a queue passes a limit.

shelves.title: Shelf availability
shelves.problem: Empty shelves are found by store walks a few times a day.
shelves.how: Cameras or phone photos spot gaps and wrong placements and create a restock task.

perimeter.title: Perimeter and after-hours intrusion
perimeter.problem: Guards watch dozens of screens and alarms fire on cats and shadows.
perimeter.how: Alarms trigger only when a person or vehicle enters a defined zone.
perimeter.kpi: false alarms per night, response time

privacy.title: Privacy-safe video
privacy.problem: Footage can’t be shared or stored because it shows faces.
privacy.how: Faces are blurred automatically before video leaves the site.

vehicleCount.title: Vehicle counting and classification
vehicleCount.problem: Traffic and parking counts are done by hand on a few days a year.
vehicleCount.how: Cameras count cars, trucks and buses by direction and hour, all year.

plates.title: Number plate recognition
plates.problem: Gate staff write plates down and check passes by eye.
plates.how: Plates are read at the gate and checked against the allowed list automatically.
plates.kpi: gate time per vehicle, unauthorised entries

driverFatigue.title: Driver and operator fatigue
driverFatigue.problem: Long shifts on trucks, buses and forklifts lead to microsleep accidents.
driverFatigue.how: An in-cab camera watches eye closure and yawning and warns the driver and dispatcher.

waybills.title: Waybill and invoice capture
waybills.problem: Staff retype invoices and waybills in Uzbek, Russian and English.
waybills.how: OCR reads the documents and fills the fields in 1C or your ERP for a person to confirm.

grading.title: Fruit and vegetable grading
grading.problem: Produce is sorted by hand, so grades vary from shift to shift.
grading.how: Cameras grade each item by size, colour and blemishes and steer it to the right lane.

livestock.title: Livestock counting
livestock.problem: Animals are counted by hand at gates and in pens.
livestock.how: Cameras count animals passing a gate and track headcount per pen.

bakery.title: Baked goods quality
bakery.problem: Burnt or underbaked items are sorted out by eye at the end of the oven.
bakery.how: A camera grades each item by colour and shape as it leaves the oven.

falls.title: Fall detection in care settings
falls.problem: A fall at night may go unnoticed for hours.
falls.how: Pose estimation spots a fall and alerts staff, without recording identifiable video.
